verdict.justification: B is the stronger senior-review draft because it identifies a potentially material excess retirement-plan deferral that A incorrectly dismisses as having no effect on the return. B quantifies the possible excess as $3,406.43 and requests confirmation before filing, whereas A says the illegible W-2 code “does not change the return.” B also flags the unusual wash-sale adjustment on Lisa’s otherwise profitable sale and more closely follows the 2024 Schedule 2 structure; A reverses the AMT and premium-tax-credit repayment lines. Both reach the same provisional $15,379 balance due and appropriately identify the unresolved Texas sales-tax deduction, but neither supplies a filing-ready return because both use custom facsimiles and leave material review items unresolved. B does have a completion defect: its Schedule 3 shows the foreign-tax-credit and dependent-care-credit descriptions without their individual amounts, despite carrying their $539 total. On balance, B’s better identification and quantification of substantive tax risks makes it more useful to the reviewing senior accountant.
